replacements.note: VERIFIED: $language is NOT in scope here. Core passes it only to views/frontend/app.blade.php (the SPA shell) from Frontend\Document; the basic layout is rendered by Foundation\ErrorHandling\ViewFormatter, which passes only `error` and `message` (core 1.8.5 src/Foundation/ErrorHandling/ViewFormatter.php:54-60). `flarum.locales` is the container alias for Flarum\Locale\LocaleManager (src/Locale/LocaleServiceProvider.php:38) and getLocale() proxies the translator, which SetLocale middleware has already set for this request. Equivalent and shorter: {{ $translator->getLocale() }} — $translator is shared into every view (Forum/ForumServiceProvider.php:147, Frontend/FrontendServiceProvider.php:175) and Flarum\Locale\Translator extends Symfony's, which has getLocale().

deferred.string: "description": "Face and body ratings, and the guides behind them."  (also "name" / "short_name")
deferred.reason: A static JSON file served straight off disk, so it has exactly one language. It is user-visible: Chrome and Safari show `name` and `description` in the install prompt and in the app listing after install. Making it per-locale means serving it from a controller (an Extend\Routes entry returning a JsonResponse built from the translator, with the <link rel="manifest"> in Head.php pointing at that route) — a new route and a new class, outside this lane. `name` and `short_name` are the brand and stay English either way; only `description` actually needs it.

Not a hardcoded string — it comes from the settings table, which holds one value for the whole forum. So the meta description, og:description and twitter:description are permanently in whichever language the admin typed. Fixing it is a settings-level concern (a per-locale forum_description, or falling back to a translation key when the setting is empty), not a code replacement, and it belongs to whoever owns the admin settings surface.

notes.blade_translator: This lane emits app('translator') as the brief specifies, and it works: app() is defined in Flarum's own framework/core/src/helpers.php. Two facts the applier may want before standardising, though. (1) $translator is ALREADY shared into every view — Forum/ForumServiceProvider.php:147 and Frontend/FrontendServiceProvider.php:175 both call $view->share(['translator' => …]) — and core's own views/error/not_found.blade.php uses {{ $translator->trans(...) }}, so the shorter form is not wrong here, it is the house style of the file being overridden. (2) core marks app() '@deprecated perpetually … should NOT be used in extension code' and offers resolve() as the supported helper. Any of the three resolves the same singleton; if the six lanes are being normalised, $translator is the one core itself uses in exactly these files.
